name: Philosophy of Mind and Cognition
description: What are the foundational issues that emerge when we investigate the nature of mental phenomena and explain the mechanisms responsible for cognition? This course offers a set of philosophical perspectives and techniques to understand these issues in a conceptually meaningful way. What constitutes a good explanation of cognitive capacities? Can behaviour and cognitive processes be understood independently of neural activity in the brain? How can we inquire about the nature of consciousness? What is the relationship between our cognitive and social capacities? Does thinking happen in a kind of language? The course examines these and other questions which underlie contemporary debates about minds and cognition.
